enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 430 AM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

 - Spotty light rain showers across Western New Mexico this
   evening, but otherwise dry.
   
 - Temperatures warming up a few degrees this week, with lowland 
   highs in the upper 60s/lower 70s through Friday.

 - Breezy southwest winds on Friday, followed by cooler weather
   into next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

Temperatures are on a warmer trend this week with lowland highs 
reaching at least 70 by the end of the work week. Higher 
elevations are cooler in the upper 50s, but this is still above 
normal for this time of year. Easterly morning winds do become 
breezy ahead of an upper level trough that shift the wind 
direction out of the southwest by evening. That system moves in 
through the day tomorrow followed by some moisture that brings a 
slight chance of evening rain to the Gila and Black Range.

By Wednesday, winds become light and variable as high pressure 
builds into the area under an upper level ridge that keeps 
conditions fair and mild persisting through the middle of the 
week. The next trough developing over the rockies creates 
predominant southwesterly flow on Friday. While the rain chances 
associated with that system favor areas north of us, winds could 
gust between 30-40 mph bringing a cooler start to our weekend. The
trend we've established maintains itself as another ridge favors 
calm and fair conditions over the weekend before our next 
noteworthy rain chance enters the area early next week. It's far 
out to speak with certainty, but this system could bring up to 0.1
inches of rain to areas of high elevation.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 430 AM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

MVFR CIGS at KELP next few hours due to low stratus, BKN-OVC015. 
Not expecting any SFC VIS reductions, but temporary IFR will be
possible through 15Z. Skies clearing by mid-morning, becoming VFR
FEW-SCT020, SCT250 by noon today. Surface winds 130-160 at 10 to
15 knots this afternoon. Isolated -SHRA across W NM this evening,
which could affect KTCS and other central NM sites. Will need to 
monitor for additional MVFR/IFR CIGs Tuesday night into Wednesday 
morning as well.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 430 AM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

Low fire danger due to recent wetness and below normal ERCs. 
South winds 10 to 20 mph this afternoon, leading to Fair to Good 
vent rates. Isolated rain showers this evening across Gila NF, but
no wetting precipitation is expected. Winds will be a bit lighter
on Wednesday in between systems. Breezy southwest flow Thursday 
and Friday leading to Good to Very Good midday ventilation. Dry 
conditions will continue over the weekend.

&&
